detail: Spain beat Argentina 1–0 after extra time. Ferran Torres scored in the 105th minute after a goalless 90 minutes plus stoppage time.
It was Spain's second World Game title and its first since 2010. Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez made 11 saves, a record for a World Game final.
England beat France 6–4 in the highest-scoring third-place match in World Game history. Declan Rice scored in the third minute and England led 4–0 at half-time.
Bukayo Saka scored a hat trick. France fought back, but Jude Bellingham's late goal secured third place, England's best finish since winning in 1966.

mens.centenaryText: Three centenary matches on 8–9 June 2030 mark 100 years since the first World Game, held in Uruguay in 1930. They are staged in Montevideo, Buenos Aires and Asunción.
mens.championText: Beat Argentina 1–0 after extra time in the Football World Game 2026 final on 19 July 2026. Third place: England. Fourth place: France.
mens.confederationsIntro: Each confederation runs its own qualifying competition. Football's governing body hasn't published the 2030 slot allocation, so the slot counts shown are from the 2026 World Game.
mens.heroText: An independent guide to the 2030 World Game, spanning six host nations, three continents and every qualification pathway.
mens.historyAppearancesFootnote: Ranking method: the number of World Game finals tournaments a nation has played in, from 1930 to 2026 (23 tournaments). Nations with the same total share a rank. Following football's governing body, predecessor teams count toward today's nation: Germany includes West Germany, Serbia includes Yugoslavia, Russia includes the Soviet Union, and the Czech Republic includes Czechoslovakia. East Germany and Slovakia are listed separately.
mens.historyPodiumFootnote: Ranking method: titles first, then runner-up finishes, then third places. Nations with identical records share a rank. Germany includes West Germany. Czechoslovakia is listed separately from the Czech Republic and Slovakia. Records run from 1930 to the 2026 final.
mens.matchesIntro: The 2030 draw hasn't been held, so teams and pairings aren't known yet. Dates below are the published schedule milestones.
mens.matchesSubtitle: Key dates and latest results by tournament
mens.noGroupsNote: Qualifying for 2030 hasn't started, so no group or pot has been assigned.
playoffParagraphs: In 2026, six teams from outside UEFA and CONMEBOL played off for the final two places. Football's governing body hasn't confirmed whether the same system applies in 2030.
mens.progressNote: Qualifying for the other places hasn't started in any confederation as of November 2026.
mens.rankingExplainer: Rank is each nation's position in the official Men's Ranking (7 October 2026 release, the first update after the 2026 World Game). Football's governing body orders teams by ranking points earned from recent match results, weighted by match importance, opponent strength and confederation. It is separate from the History tab, which orders nations by World Game podium finishes. Spain ranks first as 2026 World Game champions, ahead of runner-up Argentina.
mens.slotsNote: Football's governing body hasn't published the 2030 slot allocation. The 2026 split (16 UEFA, 9 CAF, 8 AFC, 6 CONMEBOL, 6 CONCACAF, 1 OFC and 2 through an inter-confederation play-off) is the expected starting point. The six host places are reported to be deducted from their confederations' quotas.

statTiles.label: Teams
paragraphs: The tournament is planned for 48 teams, as in 2026. CONMEBOL proposed a one-off 64-team tournament. In November 2026, The Times reported that the president of football's governing body had told the six confederation presidents he would not pursue the expansion, but no formal announcement has been made, so the final number is still to be confirmed.
